full_judgment:
2. Facts are interesting. Two suits for Specific Performance of Contract were filed. T.S. No. 33 of 1974 was instituted by Abdul Khaleque against Jonab Ali and Ali Haider. Then Ali Haider brought the T.S. No. 114 of 1974 against Jonah Ali. The trial court decreed Abdul Khaleque's suit for specific performance of contract and dismissed the suit of Ali Haider. Ali Haider unsuccessfully preferred an appeal before the High Court Division. Leave was granted to consider whether the trial court ought to have returned the consideration money to the unsuccessful plaintiff, namely Ali Haider under section 19, of the Specific Act. Relief Thus it is on a very short point, the matter came before this Court for consideration. 

 Therefore, genuineness and validity of the contract dated 10.10.73 having been not proved the learned Subordinate Judge refused a decree in favour of Ali Haider. This does not however automatically mean that the claim of Ali Haider was proved". 

 5. Mr. M. H. Khondker submitted that the High Court Division has made a conflicting observation because section 19 contemplates an existence of a contract whereas section 29 raises a bar when a suit for specific performance of contract is dismissed and the High Court Division had fallen into an error in not noticing the bar. Mr. Khondker submitted that the existence of contract could not be doubted by an appellate Court when no issue was ever framed nor the point was agitated in any Court below. It may be noticed that Jonab Ali, defendant did not contest the suit at all. So the question whether Ali Haider had paid the money could not be decided against him when there is no denial. This being, essentially a question of fact an issue ought to have been framed. It would have been different had the case been contested but Jonab Ali did not do so. He made another contract with Abdul Khaleque and that suit was decreed what will happen to the claim of, Ali Haider? The question, is whether he had, at all paid money but Jonab Ali did not appear to contest. From such a situation no inference can be drawn which is a question of fact namely whether he paid money. This requires determination on evidence.
